summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expansion for the power-conversion-equipment node found one obvious reference leader and three underfollowed or less-obvious US-listed candidates. The strongest direct small/mid-cap match is Powell Industries, which supplies engineered electrical-energy distribution and medium-voltage switchgear and has explicitly tied opportunities to data-center and AI power demand. nVent is a larger but still less-discussed electrical connection/protection platform whose Avail Electrical Products Group acquisition added switchgear, bus systems, and power-utility/data-center infrastructure exposure. Preformed Line Products is not a transformer or switchgear maker, but it is a low-attention second-order grid hardware candidate tied to transmission and distribution construction. Hubbell is included as the reference leader for utility T&D, substation, connectors, grid protection, and electrical infrastructure context. This Layer 1B pass expands the universe around a supply-chain choke point in energy infrastructure: boring but schedule-critical electrical hardware that sits between generation and load. The two-lane screen leans on obvious reference names for context, but prioritizes underfollowed mid/small-cap suppliers where long qualification cycles, limited substitutes, and capacity constraints can create backlog-driven earnings leverage. Claims below are tagged by evidence strength; several candidates are hypotheses that need direct company filing/contract verification before later layers.
